searchText: i'd support moving our pyrmont "position" to "unsupported, it just does what it does now" users can run or not but it frees up everyone to release resources etc EF and teams hold tons of validators on Pyrmont, I suggest before clients "stop supporting" it, that they exercise a massive exit queue, just to see if something breaks down. If it doesn't immediately and it seems that it's going to continue finalizing (I don't know if it is) then it's fine to simply turn those off. Hey everyone I am helping in the creation of a new Ethereum casino and we need to run the beta version on testnet, but we can't find non-stingy testnet faucets would anyone be willing to spare 50 or 100 testnet Ethers? it would be of great help I'm mostly interested in shutting down the nodes we run to save money, but I think even just one client team stopping their nodes breaks finality on pyrmont these days. I guess it could be fun to exit them all then shut down...
